## Where would you like to begin?

Artificial intelligence is reshaping how scholars learn and conduct their research. The EUI's Department of Social and Political Sciences has sponsored two Part-time Assistant Professor positions to help the community adopt AI responsibly and effectively.

On this website, you can book a consultation about your research project and find guidance and resources on AI. If you feel something is missing, please leave an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/RobertoValli/eui-ai-resources/issues/new).

::: {.home-section}
## Four principles to carry with you

::: {.principles-grid}
::: {.principle}
### You remain responsible

AI can assist with a task, but responsibility for what you submit, publish, or use in an analysis remains yours.
:::

::: {.principle}
### Protect sensitive material

Check confidentiality, consent, data-protection, and service-provider conditions before sharing research material with a tool.
:::

::: {.principle}
### Verify the output

Fluent answers can still be wrong. Check factual claims, references, summaries, code, and transformations against appropriate sources or tests.
:::

::: {.principle}
### Document consequential uses

When AI contributes to research outputs or methods, keep enough information to explain, assess, and where possible reproduce what you did.
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.home-section #about-this-resource}
## About this resource

This website is maintained independently by [Filip Olsson](https://www.eui.eu/people?id=filip-olsson) and [Roberto Valli](https://www.eui.eu/people?id=roberto-valli), the EUI Part-time Assistant Professors of AI. It is intended for EUI researchers and brings together practical advice, consultation information, and links to authoritative EUI sources.

The site complements—not replaces—formal EUI policies, your supervisor's guidance, or advice from the relevant EUI services. Where a statement summarises an institutional rule, the source is identified so that you can consult it directly.
:::
